input:
/home/eval/shop/data/orders.json is an array of shop orders. Build per-customer rollups with jq.

Rules:
- Customer key: .customer.id. Orders whose customer is null or missing belong to the key "guest".
- Only orders with status "paid" count towards paid_orders, revenue_cents, by_month and top_skus (refunded and pending orders are ignored there), but every customer key that appears in any order gets a file.
- Line revenue in cents = floor(qty * unit_cents * (100 - discount_pct) / 100), where a null or missing discount_pct means 0.
- name = .customer.name on that customer's most recent order of any status (by .placed); null for "guest".

Write one file per customer key, /home/eval/shop/out/customers/<key>.json, containing one object with exactly these keys in this order:
  customer (the key), name, paid_orders (number of paid orders), revenue_cents (integer sum of line revenue over paid orders), by_month (object mapping "YYYY-MM" of .placed to that month's revenue, keys ascending, only months with paid orders), top_skus (array of up to 3 skus with the highest revenue over paid orders, ties broken by sku ascending)
Also write /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json: an array of {"customer": <key>, "revenue_cents": <int>} for every customer key, sorted by revenue_cents descending then customer ascending.

Format every file exactly as `jq .` pretty-prints it (2-space indent, one trailing newline). Numbers must be integers (no 12.0).

transcript.final_response: Created the per-customer JSON files in `/home/eval/shop/out/customers/` and `/home/eval/shop/out/summary.json`. All files are pretty-printed JSON with a trailing newline.
tool_calls: jq -r '[.[] | (if (.customer == null or (.customer|not)) then "guest" else .customer.id end)] | unique[]' /home/eval/shop/data/orders.json; jq -r '[.[] | select(.customer != null) | .customer.id] | unique | .[]' /home/eval/shop/data/orders.json; jq --version

mkdir -p /home/eval/shop/out/customers
cat > /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.jq <<'JQ'
def customer_key:
  if .customer == null then "guest" else .customer.id end;
def item_revenue:
  ((.qty * .unit_cents * (100 - (.discount_pct // 0)) / 100) | floor);
def order_revenue:
  ([.items[]? | item_revenue] | add // 0);

[ .[] | . + { _key: customer_key } ]
| group_by(._key)
| map(
    . as $orders
    | ($orders | map(select(.status == "paid"))) as $paid
    | {
        customer: $orders[0]._key,
        name: (if $orders[0]._key == "guest" then null else ($orders | sort_by(.placed) | last | .customer.name // null) end),
        paid_orders: ($paid | length),
        revenue_cents: ([$paid[] | order_revenue] | add // 0),
        by_month: (
          [$paid[] | {month: .placed[0:7], revenue: order_revenue}]
          | group_by(.month)
          | map({key: .[0].month, value: (map(.revenue) | add // 0)})
          | sort_by(.key)
          | from_entries
        ),
        top_skus: (
          [$paid[] | .items[]? | {sku, revenue: item_revenue}]
          | group_by(.sku)
          | map({sku: .[0].sku, revenue: (map(.revenue) | add // 0)})
          | sort_by([(-.revenue), .sku])
          | .[:3]
          | map(.sku)
        )
      }
  )
JQ
jq -f /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.jq /home/eval/shop/data/orders.json > /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.tmp && mv /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.tmp /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.json
jq '[.[] | {customer, revenue_cents}] | sort_by([(-.revenue_cents), .customer])' /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.json | jq . > /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json
while IFS= read -r key; do
  jq --arg key "$key" '.[] | select(.customer == $key)' /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.json | jq . > "/home/eval/shop/out/customers/$key.json"
done < <(jq -r '.[].customer' /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.json)
ls -l /home/eval/shop/out /home/eval/shop/out/customers
cat /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json
cat /home/eval/shop/out/customers/c-bob.json

rm -f /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.jq /home/eval/shop/out/rollups.json
for f in /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json /home/eval/shop/out/customers/*.json; do jq -e . "$f" >/dev/null || exit 1; done
find /home/eval/shop/out -type f | sort
jq -r 'keys | join(",")' /home/eval/shop/out/customers/c-bob.json; tail -c 1 /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json | od -An -t x1
